note: Ps105 covenant-history hymn (45v, 174 spans). Read by CHAR-ARC. Arcs: A worship-call v1-6 (give-thanks/call/known/sing/sing-praises/tell/glory/seek-hearts/rejoice/seek/seek/remember); B patriarch-sojourners v12+v23; C Joseph's affliction->wisdom v18-22 (HURT with fetters -> at his PLEASURE, TEACH elders wisdom); D Egyptians' hearts turned to HATE + DEAL-CRAFTILY v25; E Moses/Aaron did not REBEL v28; F Egypt GLAD + DREAD at the Exodus v38; G redemption JOY + SINGING -> KEEP/OBSERVE statutes -> PRAISE v43-45. Between = God's covenant ACTS (qualifiers) + plague/Exodus imagery (standalone).

dims.v: paired with calling on his name and making known his deeds
v1: 'Oh GIVE THANKS (yadah) to the LORD' - the summons that opens the covenant-hymn, gratitude for God's faithfulness.
v1: 'CALL (qara) upon his name' - the invoking of God, worship as appeal to his name.
v1: 'make KNOWN (yada) his deeds among the peoples!' - the proclaiming of God's works to the nations, worship as witness.
paired with singing praises and telling his works
v2: 'SING (shir) to him' - the sung praise of God's covenant faithfulness.
v2: 'SING PRAISES (zamar) to him' - the melody of worship.
v2: 'TELL (siach) of all his wondrous works!' - the recounting of God's marvels, worship as rehearsal.
v3: 'GLORY (halal) in his holy name' - the exulting in God's name, boasting in him rather than self.
v3: 'let the HEARTS (leb) of those who seek the LORD rejoice!' - the inner self of the seekers gladdened, joy seated in the heart.
v3: 'the hearts of those who SEEK (baqash) the LORD' - the pursuit of God, the disposition of the true worshipper.
v3: 'let the hearts of those who seek the LORD REJOICE (samach)!' - the gladness of those who seek God, joy as seeking's reward.
v4: 'SEEK (darash) the LORD and his strength' - the resolute seeking of God, worship as constant pursuit.
v4: 'SEEK (baqash) his presence continually!' - the unceasing seeking of God's face.
paired with the wondrous works and covenant
v5: 'REMEMBER (zakar) the wondrous works that he has done' - the deliberate recalling of God's deeds, the hinge into the covenant-recital.
paired with being few in number
v12: 'When they were few in number, and SOJOURNERS (gur) in it' - the pilgrim status of the patriarchs, strangers in the land of promise.
v23: 'Jacob SOJOURNED (gur) in the land of Ham' - Israel a stranger in Egypt, the sojourning renewed a generation on.
paired with his exaltation to bind princes at his pleasure
v18: 'His feet were HURT (anah) with fetters' - Joseph's affliction in the pit of slavery, the low point before the exaltation.
paired with his affliction and his teaching
v22: 'to bind his princes at his PLEASURE (nephesh)' - Joseph's own will and discretion, the authority given the once-fettered slave.
paired with binding princes at his pleasure
v22: 'and TEACH (chakam) his elders wisdom' - Joseph the wise, instructing Egypt's counsellors, affliction turned to influence.
paired with the hatred and craft
v25: 'He turned their HEARTS (leb) to hate his people' - the Egyptians' inner disposition turned against Israel, hearts bent to enmity.
v25: 'to HATE (sane) his people' - the enmity of the Egyptians, hatred as the ground of the oppression.
v25: 'to DEAL CRAFTILY (nakal) with his servants' - the cunning malice of the Egyptians, hatred turned to calculated oppression.
v28: 'they did not REBEL (marah) against his words' - the obedience of Moses and Aaron, faithful agents who did not resist God's commission.
paired with the dread that fell on them
v38: 'Egypt was GLAD (samach) when they departed' - the relief of the Egyptians at Israel's exit, gladness born of terror.
v38: 'for DREAD (pachad) of them had fallen upon Egypt' - the terror of the Egyptians after the plagues, fear that made them glad to see Israel go.
v43: 'So he brought his people out with JOY (sason)' - the exultation of the redeemed at the Exodus, deliverance crowned with joy.
v43: 'his chosen ones with SINGING (rinnah)' - the song of the redeemed, joy voiced in praise.
v45: 'that they might KEEP (shamar) his statutes' - the purpose of the whole redemption: an obedient people, deliverance issuing in law-keeping.
v45: 'and OBSERVE (natsar) his laws' - the guarding of God's laws, the covenant's intended fruit in the redeemed.
v45: 'PRAISE (halal) the LORD!' - the closing Hallelujah, the covenant-history sealed with praise.
